newsitem.title: USA: Albright favorite to succeed Christopher.
newsitem.headline: Albright favorite to succeed Christopher.

text.p: Madeleine Albright, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, emerged on Wednesday as the clear favourite to succeed Warren Christopher as U.S. Secretary of State, U.S. officials said.

But as speculation swirled in Washington over President Bill Clinton's selection for this and other key Cabinet posts for his second term, the White House said he had not made a final decision and no announcement was expected on Wednesday.

Albright, 59, the daughter of a Czechoslovak diplomat who moved to the United States after the Second World War, has been Washington's U.N. representative since February 1993. She would be the first woman to become U.S. Secretary of State.

The president has met with top advisers and consulted by telephone as he completes the team that will help him shape foreign policy over the next four years. Diplomats said he had a telephone conversation with Albright on Tuesday, but they did not know the substance of the call.

A U.S. official said Clinton had narrowed his list for Secretary of State to Albright and former Assistant Secretary of State Richard Holbrooke, chief architect of the Bosnia peace accords, but was leaning toward Albright.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told Reuters: "The president has not made any final decision. I do not anticipate an announcement today." The choice was part of a larger process that was also expected to include the naming of a new defence secretary and possibly a new national security adviser and CIA director.
